items.headline: Tanker hits river cruise boat in New Orleans
items.summary: A tanker struck a river cruise boat carrying 129 passengers on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday, partially submerging it. Rescue operations were underway, officials said.

items.headline: Supreme Court to weigh Trump asylum ban
items.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to consider President Trump's executive order suspending asylum access at the southern border. Lower courts had ruled that blocking asylum applications there was illegal.

items.headline: Ukraine launches massive drone strike as Europe joins talks
items.summary: Ukraine fired nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war. European Council President Antonio Costa said EU officials and five Coalition of the Willing members will represent Europe at the U.S.-led peace talks.

items.headline: Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for Senate leader
items.summary: Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen said he will run for Senate majority leader in the next Congress, challenging Chuck Schumer. He also outlined plans to use Democrats' new power on foreign aid and global health.

items.headline: Bessent blames Commerce over Nvidia chip sales to China
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent faulted Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to restrict Nvidia chip sales to China. Lutnick faces scrutiny over his ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

items.headline: Navy quietly fires commanders, drawing pushback
items.summary: The Navy has fired some commanders and other officials without announcing it, a departure from its usual practice. Members of Congress have criticized the secrecy.

items.headline: Pochettino leaves USMNT for Manchester United
items.summary: Manchester United named Mauricio Pochettino its manager, ending his tenure as U.S. men's national team coach. He led the U.S. to the World Cup round of 16.

items.headline: SpaceX prepares to retire NASA's main ride to ISS
items.summary: As it develops its giant Starship rocket, SpaceX is preparing to retire the spacecraft that serves as NASA's main ride to the International Space Station. The shift raises questions about NASA's reliance on the company.

items.headline: Countries raise climate ambition despite U.S. retreat
items.summary: Experts say several countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America are strengthening their climate policies. The shift comes as the United States scales back its own climate measures.

items.headline: Early polar vortex and El Niño to shape winter
items.summary: An early polar vortex disruption combined with a strong El Niño could influence U.S. winter weather. TIME explains what the pattern may mean for the season ahead.

digest.overview:
A tanker struck a river cruise boat carrying 129 passengers on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday, partially submerging it. The Supreme Court agreed to consider President Trump's executive order suspending asylum access at the southern border after lower courts found it illegal. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department for not restricting Nvidia chip sales to China, as Lutnick faces scrutiny over his ties to Jensen Huang. The Navy has quietly fired some commanders and officials, drawing pushback from Congress. Democrats preparing to take control of Congress in January are weighing oversight, and possibly impeachment, of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Mauricio Pochettino left the U.S. men's soccer team to manage Manchester United.

Abroad, Ukraine fired nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, and European Council President Antonio Costa said EU officials and five Coalition of the Willing members will join the U.S.-led peace talks. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a liquefied gas carrier caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and Türkiye and Qatar signed a mutual defense agreement. South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met Chinese counterpart Wang Yi in Beijing, where Wang briefed him on Kim Jong Un's October visit to Dandong and Cho urged China to help bring North Korea back to dialogue. A truck-bus crash in India's Assam state killed at least 24 people. Norway lost a landmark climate case, meaning emissions from exported oil must be weighed when licensing oilfields. U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres called for immediate and drastic emissions cuts.

home.overview:
San Antonio stretched its winning streak to 11 by routing the Curry-less Warriors 123–85 in NBA Cup play, the Clippers edged Oklahoma City 113–112 despite 40 points from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Indiana held off the Knicks 106–104 to drop New York to 0-2 in its Cup group. Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks with an oblique tear. In the NFL, Baltimore's Lamar Jackson had thumb surgery and is expected to miss 6–10 weeks, leaving Jacoby Brissett to start Monday night against the Chargers. Sunday opens with Patriots-Lions in Munich, Fernando Mendoza, Carson Beck and Kyle McCord make their first starts, and Steelers-Bengals closes the night. In baseball, Jake Bauers reportedly agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with the Red Sox, and qualifying-offer decisions are due Tuesday.

Manchester United made Mauricio Pochettino their manager, though he will coach the USMNT in both Concacaf Nations League legs against Haiti, starting tonight in Miami. Germany beat nine-man Serbia 3–1 to relegate them, the Netherlands thrashed Greece 7–0 to set up Monday's decider in Berlin, Uruguay won 2–1 at La Bombonera, and South Korea fell 3–2 to Saudi Arabia in Doha. Portugal host Denmark tonight before Sunday's Spain-England showdown in Madrid, and K League 1 and 2 resume Nov. 21–22. In the KBO, free-agent negotiations open Tuesday, with 28 players eligible.

brief: South Korea lost 9–5 to Japan on Friday at Tokyo Dome to fall to 0–2 at the Asia Professional Baseball Championship.
Korea tied the game 5–5 in the top of the eighth, but Rui Muneyama's three-run homer in the bottom half put Japan ahead for good; Korea allowed four home runs.
To reach a third straight final, Korea must beat Taiwan on Saturday night and needs Japan to beat Australia, with a tiebreaker then deciding Japan's opponent in Sunday's final.
Of the 28 KBO players eligible for free agency, 15 are eligible for the first time, and KT Wiz and SSG have six each.
Eligible players have until Sunday to declare, with the final list due Monday and negotiations with any club opening Tuesday.

brief: Jake Bauers, the NLCS MVP who hit 26 homers for champion Milwaukee, reportedly agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with the Red Sox.

Because Bauers turned down a qualifying offer, Milwaukee gets a compensation pick after the first round, while Boston forfeits its second- and fifth-highest 2027 picks and $1 million in international bonus money.
Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander apologized for sharing anti-Muslim videos after GM Ross Atkins publicly criticized the posts.
The Dodgers are set to meet with top free agent Tarik Skubal, though no agreement has been reported.
The other seven qualifying-offer recipients have until Tuesday, Nov. 17, to decide on the $23.15 million offers, and the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1.

brief: Manchester United named Mauricio Pochettino their manager on Friday, a day after firing Michael Carrick, and he will coach both USMNT quarterfinal legs against Haiti before taking over on Nov. 18.
Germany beat nine-man Serbia 3–1 in Belgrade, relegating Serbia, and a win over the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday would send Jürgen Klopp's side through.
The Netherlands routed Greece 7–0 in Amsterdam to set up that decider in Berlin.
Uruguay won 2–1 at La Bombonera in Argentina's first match since Lionel Messi's international retirement, with Julián Álvarez scoring Argentina's only goal.

Portugal host Denmark tonight with Bernardo Silva as captain after Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement, while the U.S. meet Haiti in Miami and Spain host England on Sunday.
Club play returns next week, with MLS wild-card games on Nov. 19 and K League 1 and 2 resuming Nov. 21–22.
